items.prompt: With no cookie set, a client sends the header "Authorization: Bearer user-admin" to the live .NET API. Who does CurrentUser say is calling?
distractors: Nobody: the token must be a signed JWT
Nobody until the cookie is set by login
The seeded CLIENT_ADMIN, Casey Client
items.explanation: CurrentUser takes the cookie value or, failing that, whatever follows "Bearer ", and looks it up as a user id. "user-admin" is the seeded platform admin's id, so presenting it is enough to become that user.

items.prompt: A request carries the cookie globalhire_user_id=user-client and also the header "Authorization: Bearer user-admin". Which user does CurrentUser resolve?
items.answer: Casey Client, since the cookie is read first and the header skipped
distractors: Ada Admin, since an Authorization header always overrides any cookie value
Neither: two conflicting identities make the request a 401
Ada Admin, because the more privileged of the two ids wins
items.explanation: CurrentUser only reads the Authorization header when TryGetValue finds no cookie. With the cookie present, the Bearer value is never looked at.

items.prompt: The seed creates admin@globalhire.test and client@globalhire.test without setting a Password. Which password logs in as either one?
items.answer: password123, the default on the User record
distractors: Password123!, as the README lists
None, since each account needs a password reset first
A random one printed at startup
items.explanation: User.Password defaults to "password123", and login compares the plaintext with ==. The README's Password123! belongs to the commented-out TypeScript seed.

items.prompt: A CLIENT_ADMIN of Org B sends PATCH /api/onboarding-tasks/<a task belonging to an Org A worker>/approve. What happens?
items.answer: It is APPROVED, with the Org B admin recorded as reviewer
distractors: 403, as the task belongs to a worker in another organization
404, since Org B cannot even see Org A's onboarding tasks
400, because a task must be SUBMITTED before it is approved
items.explanation: The approve handler checks only that the actor is not a WORKER. It never compares organizations and never checks the current task status, so the approval goes through.

items.prompt: Worker Maya submits a leave request, then calls PATCH /api/leave-requests/<her request>/approve with her own session. What does ReviewLeave do?
items.answer: Approves it, recording Maya as the reviewer
distractors: Returns 403, since workers cannot review requests
Returns 409, because a reviewer must differ from the requester
Approves it, but flags it for a manager to confirm
items.explanation: ReviewLeave authorises with CanAccessWorker, which is true when a WORKER actor's WorkerId matches the worker. There is no reviewer-role check, so Maya approves her own leave.

items.prompt: A worker is ONBOARDING with unapproved tasks and an unsigned contract. A CLIENT_ADMIN of the same org sends PATCH /api/workers/<id> with {"status":"ACTIVE"}. What is the result?
items.answer: The worker becomes ACTIVE, skipping every activation check
distractors: 400, as the onboarding tasks must be approved before activation
400: the contract must be SIGNED before activation
403: status changes are allowed only via /activate
items.explanation: WorkerService.Update applies input.Status whenever it is present. The checks on tasks and contract live only in Activate, so the generic PATCH bypasses them (mass assignment).

items.prompt: An offboarding case is REQUESTED. A CLIENT_ADMIN of the worker's org calls PATCH /api/offboarding-cases/<id>/COMPLETED. What happens to the case and the worker?
items.answer: The case is COMPLETED and the worker is TERMINATED at once
distractors: 400, as a REQUESTED case cannot jump straight to COMPLETED
The case is COMPLETED, but the worker stays OFFBOARDING
403, since only an EOR specialist may complete a case
items.explanation: The handler takes any OffboardingStatus from the URL, checks only CanAccessWorker, sets the status, and terminates the worker whenever the new status is COMPLETED. There are no transition rules.

items.prompt: An ACTIVE Canadian worker earns 4,800 per period (CA rule: employee tax 0.20, employer cost 0.14). In the period she has one APPROVED timesheet with 8 overtime hours and one SUBMITTED timesheet with 6. What gross and net pay does Calculate store?
distractors: Gross 4,800.00 and net 3,840.00
Gross 5,430.00 and net 4,344.00
Gross 5,160.00 and net 4,437.60
items.explanation: Only APPROVED timesheets count, so 8 hours. Hourly rate is 4,800 / 160 = 30; overtime pay 8 * 30 * 1.5 = 360; gross 5,160. Net is gross minus employee tax (20%, 1,032), so 4,128. Employer cost is not deducted from net.

items.prompt: Org Acme already has a USD payroll run for 1 to 30 June. A CLIENT_ADMIN creates a second run for exactly 1 to 30 June, this time in CAD. What does PayrollService.Create return?
items.answer: A new DRAFT run, as currency is part of the check
distractors: An error: a run already exists for that period
The existing USD run, returned idempotently instead
An error: the currency must match the org's
items.explanation: The duplicate check matches organization, period start, period end AND currency. A CAD run for the same dates is a different key, so it is created.

items.prompt: A worker is ONBOARDING, every required onboarding task is APPROVED, and the employment ContractStatus is SENT. An EOR specialist calls POST /api/workers/<id>/activate. What comes back?
items.answer: An error: the contract must be SIGNED first
distractors: The worker is activated, as all tasks are done
An error: only a CLIENT_ADMIN may activate
The worker is ACTIVE, with the contract flagged
items.explanation: Activate requires ONBOARDING status, no required task that is not APPROVED, and ContractStatus SIGNED. SENT fails the last check with "Employment contract must be SIGNED before activation".

items.prompt: A worker posts a leave request from 1 January 2027 to 31 December 2029. What does the live API do with it?
items.answer: Creates it, because only end-before-start is refused
distractors: Refuses it, as leave cannot exceed one calendar year in length
Refuses it, since it is longer than the statutory vacation days
Creates it, but trims the end date to the year's end
items.explanation: The handler resolves the worker, checks access, and refuses only EndDate < StartDate. There is no length, balance or statutory-days check, so a three-year leave request is stored.

items.prompt: A page using the useLoad hook fails its first fetch, and the user clicks a button that calls reload(), which now succeeds. What does the hook return afterwards?
items.answer: The new data, but the old error message is still set
distractors: The new data, and the error is cleared by the successful retry
No data: a failed hook stays failed until remount
The old data, since tick does not re-run the effect
items.explanation: reload() bumps tick, so the effect re-runs and setData stores the result. Nothing ever calls setError(""), so the first failure's message stays and the page keeps showing it.

items.front: Which two separate questions must every endpoint that takes an entity id answer?
items.back: Is this actor allowed to perform this kind of action (role), and is it allowed on this specific record (ownership or tenancy)? Checking only the first is IDOR. Write one reusable guard per entity and call it in every handler, reads and writes.

items.front: What goes wrong with the in-memory store registered as a singleton?
items.back: One instance of plain List<T>s is shared by concurrent requests, so simultaneous writes can corrupt a list. Calculate does RemoveAll then AddRange with no atomicity: a reader in between sees a calculated run with no items, and an exception in between loses them.

items.front: What is wrong with how this repo migrated from TypeScript to .NET?
items.back: The original app was kept by prefixing every line of 87 files with //, with no git history at all. Version control is what makes old code recoverable; commented-out code rots, confuses search and review, and still has to be read.

items.front: What rounding policy does PayrollService.Calculate apply, and why should it be written down?
items.back: Each payroll item is rounded to 2 decimal places, then the run totals are sums of the rounded items, so totals equal the lines a worker sees. That is defensible, but it should be a comment or a test; rounding totals independently is how invoices end up a cent off.
